report.verdict: Q3-26 was a sequential improvement (revenue +7% QoQ to $40.3m, adj. EBITDA +31% QoQ to $10.0m, margin 20%→25%) that still missed the Street by ~3–4% on revenue and fell well short of the company's own plan, forcing a FY26 guidance cut to ~$157m / ~$37m from $165–170m / $45–50m — the entire shortfall sits in consumer-facing brands (international SEO/casino affiliate and OddsJam subscriptions) while B2B (OpticOdds >50%, Grandstand Partners) grows. With $120.1m of bank debt due 2028, $27.0m of OddsJam deferred consideration due April 2027, $8.1m of cash and a post-print market cap of ~$16m, the Jefferies-led "strategic review" is first and foremost a refinancing; the equity is now a levered option on that outcome rather than on operating recovery.

summary: **Headline: a miss dressed as a sequential recovery.** Revenue $40.25m (+3% YoY reported, +5% constant currency; +7% QoQ) vs Street consensus of ~$41.3–42.0m (Zacks $41.5m, StreetInsider $41.3m, Chartmill $42.0m) — a 3–4% miss. Adj. EBITDA $10.0m (-23% YoY, +31% QoQ); adj. EBITDA margin 24.9% (-850bps YoY, +460bps QoQ). Adj. net income $5.5m (-42%); adj. EPS $0.10 diluted / $0.15 basic vs $0.26 a year ago.

**IFRS optics flatter.** Operating profit $3.8m vs a $(1.4)m loss and net income $1.0m ($0.03/share) vs $(3.9)m — but the swing is almost entirely the absence of last year's $7.5m contingent-consideration fair-value charge and $0.5m of acquisition costs, not operations. Finance expenses rose 52% to $3.8m. 9M net loss $(4.8)m, $(0.13)/share.

**Guidance cut — and it is 100% consumer-brand driven.** FY26 revenue now ~$157m (from $165–170m; -6% vs midpoint) and adj. EBITDA ~$37m (from $45–50m; -22%). The ~$10.5m revenue cut drops through ~1:1 to EBITDA. Management is explicit: enterprise data (OpticOdds) and Grandstand Partners are on plan; owned consumer brands in marketing (international SEO/casino) and data (OddsJam subscriptions) are 'performing below their potential'. FX assumption trimmed to EUR/USD 1.15 (from 1.16).

**Implied Q4-26 is the real story.** 9M revenue $118.5m / adj. EBITDA $26.7m imply Q4-26 revenue of ~$38.5m — -17% YoY against the record $46.2m Q4-25 and -4% QoQ in what is seasonally the strongest quarter — and adj. EBITDA of ~$10.3m (-33% YoY vs $15.5m; ~27% margin). At guide, FY26 = revenue -5% and adj. EBITDA -36% vs FY25 ($165.4m / $58.1m), with margin compressing from 35% to ~24%. Craig-Hallum called this out on the call; the CEO's answer was 'roughly the same drivers… but some of these are accelerating'.

**Strategic review is a refinancing first.** The Board has engaged Jefferies; the stated scope explicitly includes refinancing the $120.1m Wells Fargo facility (maturing 2028) and the $27.0m OddsJam deferred consideration due April 2027. No timetable, no further comment. CEO: the valuation 'does not reflect the strength of the business and its cash flow generation'. Given a ~$16m post-print market cap vs ~$30m of FY26 adj. FCF, that is arithmetically true — but the equity sits behind ~$139m of debt-like claims.

**Mix shift to North America / B2B is genuinely working on the top line.** North America +54% YoY to $30.4m (76% of group vs 51%); data services +17% to $10.8m (27%); sports vertical +20% to $17.9m (45% of revenue); performance marketing +7% to $25.6m; non-SEO now ~2/3 of marketing revenue. New depositing customers up QoQ and YoY (not quantified).

**International is collapsing, not softening.** UK&I -45% to $5.3m, Other Europe -51% to $3.4m, Rest of World -57% to $1.2m; international in aggregate $9.8m (-49% YoY, -14% QoQ), now 24% of revenue vs 49% a year ago. Drivers: SEO/AI-search disruption, casino LTV compression from UK remote-gaming tax step-ups that also bleeds into legacy revenue share, and a casino vertical down 11%. Management: 'we're not expecting growth in the SEO side of the business'; marketing guided 'more or less flat' 2026→2027.

**The margin problem is structural, not cyclical.** Gross margin 79.0% vs 84.3% in Q2 and 91.3% in Q3-25; cost of sales +148% YoY to $8.4m (21% of revenue vs 9%), ~$1m above internal forecast on strong partner revenue. Partner/paid traffic (Grandstand Partners) replacing zero-cost SEO carries a permanently different cost structure — the CEO's own words: 'our revenue is holding up okay. It's the margin that's coming down.'

**Cost programme is delivering, with a second round coming.** May-26 restructuring realised ~$3.25m of fixed-cost savings in Q3 vs the pre-announcement run-rate (~$6.5m in H2-26, ~$13m annualised). Opex ex-FV movements -5% YoY to $28.0m; S&M -13% to $13.9m (34% of revenue vs 41%). Restructuring cash cost $3.0m YTD ($1.85m in Q3). A further brand-portfolio consolidation and marketing-team restructuring is flagged for 2027 savings — unquantified.

**Cash conversion remains the bull case.** Adj. FCF $8.0m (80% of adj. EBITDA; 9M $21.5m, 81%); reported FCF $6.2m; OCF $7.3m. ~$30m of FY26 adj. FCF reiterated with 70–80% conversion. Q3 term-loan repayment $2.8m, interest settled $2.9m. No buybacks in the quarter; $14.4m authorisation idle — correctly so.

**Leverage is rising into a shrinking EBITDA base.** Net debt (borrowings less cash) $112.0m = 2.7x LTM adj. EBITDA of $42.2m and 3.0x FY26E; including $27.1m of deferred/contingent consideration, $139.1m = 3.3x LTM / 3.8x FY26E (our calcs; company does not publish a leverage ratio). Liquidity $32.6m (cash $8.1m + $24.5m undrawn revolver). CFO: leverage 'not alarmingly high'; covenants in compliance.

**Deferred-consideration dilution maths has become brutal.** Any proportion of the $27m OddsJam deferred payment can be settled in stock. At $0.44 that is ~61m shares vs 35.6m basic (~170% dilution); at the $0.74 pre-print close ~37m shares (~100%). The Q3 diluted share count already jumped to 53.7m (contingently issuable shares), which is why adj. EPS prints $0.10 diluted vs $0.15 basic — and why the CFO's '$0.12' on the call is inconsistent with the release.

**OpticOdds is the growth engine — but data revenue still fell QoQ.** Enterprise data grew 'well above 50%' YoY; average deal size +25% QoQ; customer count +11% QoQ; international 41% of new deals; market makers (prediction markets) ~30% of new deals. Yet total data revenue slipped 4% QoQ ($11.2m→$10.8m) and sits below the ~$12m Q4-25 level, meaning OddsJam consumer subscriptions are shrinking fast (subs down YoY, ARPU +85% as it moves upmarket). RotoWire subs +17% YoY but mix-shifting to lower-monthly-value annual plans.

**US demand signals are mixed.** iGaming, prediction markets and RotoWire cross-sell are growing; OSB operators are 'pulling back' marketing spend through the NFL season as they reset plans amid prediction-market uncertainty. Advertising & other revenue -33% YoY to $3.9m. A ~$0.5m October revenue-share hit from a single tagged-player jackpot is already in the Q4 guide.

**Rollcard (fintech) is early and small.** Launched Aug-26: cash-back-on-spend debit card for high-rollers, acquired via owned brands and the Partners network; 100% MoM growth in deposits to operators; ~$411 monthly interchange per customer. 'More meaningful' revenue only from mid-2027 — immaterial to FY26/27 numbers.

**2027 framing from management (not guidance):** revenue, adj. EBITDA and adj. FCF growth, driven by enterprise data, Grandstand Partners, Rollcard and a lower fixed-cost base; marketing flat; no SEO growth assumed; Q4-26 exit margin (~27%) to 'carry forward'. We treat this as a base case with downside skew on international and gross margin.

**One-offs and disclosure noise.** New $0.8m 'litigation costs' adjusting item (outside ordinary course, unexplained); $0.2m lease termination/PP&E write-off in restructuring; cost of sales ~$1m above forecast; FX: +3% reported vs +5% cc for Q3, -1% vs -5% cc for 9M. next.io misreported Other Europe as $4.4m (company: $3.4m).

**Street and market reaction.** Macquarie cut to Neutral, PT $3→$1; Craig-Hallum Buy, PT $6→$3; Stifel Buy, PT $5.50→$4 ('another challenging quarter'). Shares -40% intraday on 20 Nov to ~$0.44 (prior close $0.74), having already lost ~87% YTD before the print.

**Thesis read-through.** The pivot from SEO affiliate to B2B data and partner-led marketing is working on revenue but at structurally lower gross margin, while the legacy high-margin international affiliate book is eroding faster than new business can replace it in EBITDA. Rebrand (Gambling.com Group → Grandstand, ticker GAMB → GRSD, 22 Jul 2026) and the CEO transition from Charles Gillespie to Kevin McCrystle during 2026 [date unverified] complete the reset narrative; the next catalyst is the refinancing terms, not Q4 operations.

segments.name: Marketing Services (73% of revenue) — owned brands, Grandstand Partners, Rollcard
segments.headline: Revenue stabilised at -1% YoY (+11% QoQ) on North American partner, iGaming and prediction-market growth, but the SEO-to-partner mix shift has cut gross margin 1,230bps YoY to 79% and international owned brands are in free-fall.
narrative: Marketing revenue was $29.5m, down 1% year-on-year but up 11% sequentially from $26.5m — a meaningful improvement on the -10% YoY print in Q2 and, on management's framing, evidence that the diversification away from organic search is working. Performance marketing (CPA, revenue share, hybrid and ticketing) rose 7% to $25.6m and now accounts for 64% of group revenue, while advertising and other fell 33% to $3.9m as operator media budgets tightened. By vertical, casino declined 11% to $20.5m (51% of group vs 59% a year ago), sports grew 20% to $17.9m (45%) and 'other' — essentially ticketing and the early fintech line — more than doubled to $1.8m. Non-SEO channels were roughly two-thirds of marketing revenue, SEO roughly one-third, against a business that was almost entirely SEO a few years ago; total recurring revenue (subscriptions plus revenue share) was disclosed at ~50% of group in Q2 and was not updated. North American growth was led by the Grandstand Partners audience-network platform, iGaming, prediction markets and cross-selling marketing services into the RotoWire audience, and they said new depositing customers rose both quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year, although no NDC count has been disclosed. They also said marketing contribution margin improved versus Q2, without quantifying it.

The cost side is where the thesis is being tested. Cost of sales — overwhelmingly a marketing-segment cost, being revenue share paid to partner publishers and paid-traffic acquisition — rose 148% YoY and 42% QoQ to $8.4m, or 21% of group revenue against 9% a year ago, and the CFO conceded it landed roughly $1m above internal forecast on stronger-than-planned partner revenue. Group gross margin fell to 79.0% from 84.3% in Q2 and 91.3% in Q3-25. Sales and marketing expense fell 13% YoY to $13.9m, or 34% of revenue (41% in Q3-25, 43% in Q2-26), as lower people costs from the May restructuring were partly offset by higher external marketing 'tied to revenue'. The CEO's candour here was unusual and worth relaying: revenue is 'holding up okay', it is the margin that is coming down, because partner and paid channels 'have a different cost structure versus SEO'. We read this as a permanent re-basing of gross margin into the high-70s/low-80s rather than a transition cost; the bull case therefore has to rest on opex leverage and B2B data mix, not on gross-margin recovery.

On demand, the picture is bifurcated. In the US, online sportsbook operators are 'pulling back a little bit' on marketing spend through the NFL season as they reset plans amid prediction-market uncertainty — something management says it had planned for but which is 'unhelpful' — with prediction markets and iGaming largely filling the gap, and they described North American trends overall as 'really positive'. Internationally it is a convergence of negatives: continued SEO erosion, which some North American assets are weathering better than the international portfolio, multiplied by lower casino player lifetime values after tax increases that also flow through legacy revenue-share arrangements, which they admitted have 'not been as stable as we've historically seen'. Macquarie flagged the UK sports-betting duty increase due in 2027 as a further headwind; management's view is that sports is 'a little more stable' and casino 'gets hit a little harder'. Asked directly by Craig-Hallum whether the international consumer business is still worth chasing, the CEO said net new business is still a positive contribution and not loss-making, and the CFO added that portfolio and team-size optimisation should improve international owned-brand contribution margins in 2027. Management is not expecting SEO growth and guided marketing revenue 'more or less flat' from 2026 to 2027.

The response is a second restructuring layered on the May programme: streamlining brand-portfolio management toward holistic multi-channel and retention strategies across a smaller number of brands, and repositioning resources — primarily within marketing — for further 2027 cost savings that were not quantified. Rollcard, the high-roller debit card launched in August, sits in this segment as the consumer-fintech bet: acquisition comes from owned brands and the Partners network, the incentive is cash-back on spend rather than upfront bonus, deposits to operators are growing ~100% month-on-month and monthly interchange is running at ~$411 per customer, heavily skewed to high-rollers. They are extending payments capabilities and bespoke operator integrations and expect 'more meaningful' revenue from mid-2027; it is immaterial to FY26/27 numbers and we would want customer counts before ascribing value. Finally, a single tagged-player jackpot cut October revenue share by ~$0.5m — a useful reminder that revenue-share income carries operator-side variance, and that it is already embedded in the Q4 guide.

segments.name: Data Services (27% of revenue) — OpticOdds (enterprise), OddsJam & RotoWire (consumer)
segments.headline: Enterprise data (OpticOdds) is compounding at >50% with expanding deal sizes and a growing market-maker channel, but total data revenue still fell 4% QoQ because OddsJam consumer subscriptions are shrinking faster than the headline suggests.
narrative: Data services revenue — all subscription — was $10.8m, up 17% year-on-year and accelerating from +12% in Q2, taking it to 27% of group revenue from 24%; for the nine months it grew 13% to $33.2m. Enterprise sports-data services, i.e. the OpticOdds B2B odds, pricing and trading-tools business, represented a 'large majority' of data revenue and grew 'well above 50%' year-on-year. They continue to onboard new customers and, more importantly, to expand within existing ones: average deal size grew 25% sequentially, driven by larger new deals and upsell of existing customers into new features, and the total customer count grew 11% sequentially. International partners represented ~41% of new deals in the quarter and market makers — the prediction-market exchanges and liquidity providers — were ~30% of new OpticOdds deals, though still a smaller share of revenue. Management positions OpticOdds as having 'a long runway and multiple opportunities for product expansion', and in the 2027 framing, essentially all group growth is expected to come from data.

The sequential trend, however, undercuts the headline. Data revenue was ~$12.0m in Q4-25 (26% of $46.2m, +29% QoQ at the time), $11.2m in Q1-26, $11.2m in Q2-26 and $10.8m in Q3-26 — three consecutive quarters of flat-to-down against an enterprise line growing >50%. The arithmetic therefore implies consumer subscription revenue is declining at a rate well into double digits. OddsJam, the consumer positive-EV betting tool, is 'seeing a lot of increased competition from cheaper but worse alternatives' and is being deliberately repositioned upmarket as a premium product for advanced users: total subscribers are down year-on-year while ARPU is up 85%. RotoWire subscribers are up 17% year-on-year but the base is shifting hard toward annual plans — lower monthly value, higher lifetime value — which management says depressed Q3 and should show up as lower churn in 2027. The company does not disclose the enterprise/consumer split, subscriber counts or ARPU levels, so the net trajectory of the consumer book cannot be independently verified; this is the single most useful disclosure they could add.

Strategically, OpticOdds is the asset that justifies the 'intelligence layer' positioning and the one most likely to attract strategic interest in the review — its customer set spans traditional sportsbooks and the emerging market-maker ecosystem, and the deal-size expansion suggests pricing power within the installed base. The risks are those of any young B2B data vendor: customer concentration (undisclosed), the regulatory overhang on prediction markets which could impair a channel that is ~30% of new bookings, and the possibility that incumbents (Sportradar, Genius) compete harder on pricing tools. On the consumer side, the group is also trying to layer prediction-market monetisation and top-of-funnel audience products onto OddsJam users — sensible, but it is a defensive move to arrest a declining base rather than a growth story. We would model data services at mid-teens growth for FY27 with the mix moving further toward enterprise, and would treat any quarter where total data revenue falls sequentially again as a signal that consumer decay is outrunning OpticOdds.

segments.name: Geographic — North America vs International (UK&I, Other Europe, Rest of World)
segments.headline: North America +54% to $30.4m (76% of group) on partners, iGaming, prediction markets and OpticOdds; international -49% to $9.8m as SEO, casino LTVs and legacy revenue share all erode at once.
narrative: Revenue is disclosed by end-user location and includes both marketing and data. North America rose 54% year-on-year and 16% sequentially to $30.4m, taking it to 76% of group revenue from 51% a year ago and 70% in Q2; for the nine months it grew 39% to $83.3m. The growth came from the Grandstand Partners audience network, iGaming and prediction-market referrals, cross-selling into RotoWire, and the OpticOdds enterprise base, with NDCs up on both comparisons. Two caveats temper the number: the partner-led portion carries cost of sales that SEO never did, so North American growth is margin-dilutive at the gross level, and the Q3-25 base already included a full quarter of OddsJam/OpticOdds (acquired January 2025), so this is largely organic rather than acquisition-flattered — which makes it the one unambiguously good operating data point in the print. Some North American SEO assets are also reported to be holding up 'pretty well', in contrast to the international portfolio.

International, by contrast, is shrinking at a pace that is hard to describe as a transition. UK & Ireland fell 45% YoY and 17% QoQ to $5.3m (13% of group vs 25%); Other Europe fell 51% YoY and 5% QoQ to $3.4m (8% vs 18%); Rest of World fell 57% YoY and 21% QoQ to $1.2m (3% vs 6%). In aggregate international revenue was $9.8m, down 49% YoY and 14% QoQ, and 24% of group against 49% a year ago; for the nine months it is down 41% to $35.2m. Constant-currency growth at group level was +5% versus +3% reported for the quarter (and -5% versus -1% for the nine months), so FX was a modest headwind in Q3 — the international declines in constant currency are therefore marginally less severe but still in the 40s. Management attributes the collapse to a convergence: SEO rankings volatility and AI-search disruption hitting the owned casino brands hardest, lower casino player LTVs after the UK remote-gaming tax step-up (with the 2027 sports-betting duty rise still to come), and regulatory and tax effects bleeding into legacy revenue-share income that had historically been the most stable, highest-margin part of the group. Chad Beynon at Macquarie pressed on whether UK&I's deceleration was SEO or tax-driven; the answer was effectively both, multiplied together.

The strategic conclusion management drew on the call is that there are 'multiple ways to win' in North America — marketing, data, prediction markets, fintech — and 'fewer ways we monetise those audiences' internationally. They are not exiting: net new international business is still a positive contribution and not loss-making, and the legacy revenue-share annuity remains cash-generative even as it decays. But the plan is explicitly to manage the international owned brands 'for what they are now' — consolidate the brand portfolio, shrink team sizes, and lift contribution margins in 2027 — rather than to invest for growth. For modelling purposes we would assume international continues to decline at a 30–40% YoY rate through H1-27 before comps ease, that North America has to carry the entire top line, and that the group's blended gross margin keeps drifting toward the North American partner mix. One data-quality note: next.io's write-up reports Other Europe at $4.4m; the company's own disaggregation shows $3.4m, and we use the company figure.

Plan: consolidate brand portfolio, shrink team sizes, lift contribution margins in 2027 rather than invest for growth.
North America must carry the entire top line; blended gross margin keeps drifting toward North American partner mix.
Data-quality note: next.io reports Other Europe at $4.4m; company disaggregation shows $3.4m, which we use.

highlights.text: Sequential inflection delivered as promised: revenue +7% QoQ to $40.3m, adj. EBITDA +31% QoQ to $10.0m, margin +460bps to 25%, with ~$3.25m of May-restructuring savings realised in the quarter against a ~$13m annualised target; opex ex-FV -5% YoY and S&M down to 34% of revenue from 41%.

OpticOdds enterprise data growing >50% YoY with average deal size +25% QoQ, customer count +11% QoQ, 41% of new deals international and ~30% from prediction-market makers — a genuine B2B compounding asset inside a shrinking affiliate.
North America +54% YoY to $30.4m (76% of group), largely organic on a full-period OddsJam base; NDCs up QoQ and YoY; iGaming, prediction markets and Partners offsetting OSB operator budget cuts.
Cash conversion intact: adj. FCF $8.0m at 80% of adj. EBITDA (9M $21.5m, 81%); ~$30m FY26 adj. FCF reiterated — roughly twice the post-print market capitalisation.
Vertical mix moving toward sports (+20% YoY, 45% of revenue) and away from casino (-11%), which management says is more resilient to tax changes; performance marketing +7% YoY.
IFRS profitability restored — operating profit $3.8m and net income $1.0m vs losses a year ago — though largely because the $7.5m Q3-25 contingent-consideration FV charge did not recur.
Rollcard early KPIs (deposits +100% MoM, ~$411 monthly interchange per customer) suggest the high-roller fintech niche has product-market fit, with a low-cost, performance-based acquisition model.

lowlights.text: FY26 guidance cut to ~$157m / ~$37m from $165–170m / $45–50m (-6% / -22% vs midpoints) three months after being reiterated; implied Q4-26 revenue ~$38.5m is -17% YoY and -4% QoQ in the seasonally strongest quarter, and implied Q4 adj. EBITDA ~$10.3m is -33% YoY. Second consecutive November guidance cut (FY25 was also adjusted in Nov-25).

International revenue -49% YoY / -14% QoQ to $9.8m (UK&I -45%, Other Europe -51%, RoW -57%), now 24% of group vs 49%; SEO/AI-search disruption compounded by UK tax-driven casino LTV compression that is also eroding legacy revenue share. Management expects no SEO growth and flat marketing revenue in 2027.

Gross margin -1,230bps YoY to 79% (-530bps QoQ) as cost of sales rose 148% to $8.4m, ~$1m above internal forecast; the partner/paid traffic model is structurally lower-margin than SEO and adj. EBITDA margin (25%) is unlikely to return to the mid-30s of FY25.

Data revenue fell 4% QoQ to $10.8m and is below the ~$12m Q4-25 level despite OpticOdds >50% — OddsJam consumer subscriptions are shrinking (subs down YoY, ARPU +85%), and the enterprise/consumer split is not disclosed.

Balance sheet is the binding constraint: $120.1m borrowings (due 2028) plus $27.0m OddsJam deferred consideration (April 2027) against $8.1m cash; net debt 2.7x LTM adj. EBITDA ex-deferred, 3.3x including it, rising to ~3.0x/3.8x on FY26E; finance expense +52% YoY to $3.8m. Stock settlement of the deferred payment at ~$0.44 would imply ~170% dilution — hence the Jefferies refinancing mandate.

Diluted share count jumped to 53.7m from 35.6m (contingently issuable shares), cutting adj. EPS to $0.10 vs $0.15 basic; the CFO cited $0.12 on the call. A new, unexplained $0.8m 'litigation costs' adjusting item also appeared.
US OSB operators are cutting marketing spend through the NFL season; advertising & other revenue -33% YoY; a $0.5m October jackpot hit to revenue share is already in the Q4 guide.

forecast.intro: Guidance moved from FY26 revenue of $165–170m and adj. EBITDA of $45–50m (set March 2026, reiterated in May and August) to approximately $157m and $37m. The ~$10.5m midpoint revenue cut flows through almost dollar-for-dollar to EBITDA, which tells you the shortfall is in the highest-margin lines: international owned-brand affiliate revenue (SEO and casino revenue share, which carry negligible cost of sales) and OddsJam consumer subscriptions. The B2B lines — OpticOdds enterprise data and Grandstand Partners — are described as on plan, but they arrive at ~79% gross margin rather than ~91%. The other moving parts are unchanged: ~$6.5m of H2-26 fixed-cost savings from the May restructuring (~$13m annualised), initial Rollcard revenue and costs for Aug–Dec, and an average EUR/USD of 1.15 (from 1.16). Management did not give Q4 guidance explicitly, but 9M actuals imply Q4-26 revenue of ~$38.5m (-17% YoY vs the record $46.2m Q4-25; -4% QoQ) and adj. EBITDA of ~$10.3m (~27% margin; -33% YoY vs $15.5m). ~$30m of FY26 adj. FCF was reiterated at 70–80% conversion.
forecast.view: **Q4-26: achievable but with downside skew.** The implied ~$38.5m already embeds the $0.5m October jackpot hit and the OSB spend pullback; the risk is that international (-14% QoQ in Q3) decays faster than North American partners and prediction markets can offset, and that cost of sales again overshoots. Adj. EBITDA of ~$10.3m requires a full quarter of restructuring run-rate (~$3.25m/qtr) and S&M held near 34% of revenue — plausible. We would pencil in Q4 revenue of $37.5–39.0m and adj. EBITDA of $9.5–10.5m (estimate). **FY27 (our estimate, not guidance):** marketing flat at ~$112–115m per management, data +15–18% to ~$50–52m, giving revenue of ~$160–167m (+2–6%); gross margin drifting to ~78–80%; a full year of the ~$13m fixed-cost programme (~$6.5m incremental vs FY26) plus an unquantified second marketing restructuring; adj. EBITDA ~$42–47m (26–28% margin) and adj. FCF ~$30–35m. That is growth off a depressed base, not a recovery to FY25's $58m. **Leverage direction:** net debt/adj. EBITDA peaks around 3.0x (3.8x incl. deferred) at FY26 and should fall toward ~2.3–2.5x by end-27 if FCF is applied to debt — but the $27m April-27 deferred payment absorbs nearly a year of free cash flow, which is why the refinancing is non-optional. **Valuation framing:** at ~$0.44 the market cap is ~$16m and EV ~$155m, i.e. ~4.2x FY26E / ~3.5x FY27E adj. EBITDA and ~0.5x FY26 adj. FCF on the equity — the equity trades as a stub behind the credit. Plausible review outcomes range from (i) a term-out of the Wells Fargo facility plus a cash/renegotiated settlement of the deferred consideration (equity survives as a levered option on OpticOdds), to (ii) a sale of the group or of OpticOdds alone to a data or affiliate consolidator, to (iii) a dilutive stock settlement. **Swing factors:** terms and timing of the refinancing; whether international stabilises below $9m/qtr; Q4 gross margin; prediction-market regulation hitting the market-maker channel; and Nasdaq $1 minimum-bid compliance with the stock at ~$0.44.
watch: Refinancing terms (coupon, maturity, covenants) and how the $27m April-27 OddsJam deferred consideration is settled — cash, stock, or renegotiated; any stock component at sub-$1 prices is extremely dilutive.
Q4-26 actuals vs the implied ~$38.5m revenue / ~$10.3m adj. EBITDA, and specifically whether gross margin holds ~79% or slips further as partner mix rises.
International run-rate: does the -14% QoQ decline in Q3 (to $9.8m) moderate, and what does the UK 2027 sports-betting duty increase do to revenue share?

Sequential data revenue — a second QoQ decline would confirm OddsJam consumer decay is outrunning OpticOdds; push for disclosure of the enterprise/consumer split, customer concentration and subscriber counts.
US OSB operator marketing budgets into Q1-27 and the regulatory trajectory of prediction markets (CFTC/state actions), which affect both NDC referrals and ~30% of new OpticOdds bookings.
Nasdaq minimum-bid-price ($1.00) compliance — the shares have been below $1 since well before the print; a deficiency notice or reverse split would be a governance event.
Nature and size of the new 'litigation costs' adjusting item ($0.8m in Q3) and any further restructuring charges from the 2027 brand-portfolio consolidation.
Rollcard customer counts, interchange economics and any credit/fraud losses as it scales toward 'meaningful' revenue in mid-2027.

report.confidenceNote: HIGH on all reported financials: every P&L, balance-sheet, cash-flow and revenue-disaggregation figure is taken from the company's Q3-26 results release (also filed as Exhibit 99.1 to a Form 6-K), cross-checked against the Q2-26 6-K, the Q4/FY25 release and the call transcript; next.io corroborates the headline numbers (but misreports Other Europe as $4.4m vs the company's $3.4m, and rounds revenue to $40.3m vs the company's $40.2m — we use 40,250 → $40.3m). MEDIUM on consensus (three vendors: revenue $41.3–42.0m; adj. EBITDA consensus not found) and on the share-price move, which is an intraday reading (MarketScreener/Fool) rather than a verified close. Not disclosed/unverified: Q3-25 net debt; enterprise vs consumer data split; NDC counts; CEO transition date (Gillespie → McCrystle during 2026); Gaming Intelligence source URL was not accessible at fetch time. Leverage ratios, implied Q4 and FY27 figures are our calculations/estimates and labelled as such. FX: company reports in USD — no conversion applied; guidance assumes EUR/USD 1.15 average for FY26.
